Aggregate learning across participants

Source: R/fba-learning.R
aggregate_learning.Rd

Averages the per-participant proportions of correct responses within each stage, contingency type and block, and gives the standard error of that mean.

Usage

aggregate_learning(learning, silence = FALSE)

Arguments

learning

A per-participant learning summary, from score_learning().

silence

Logical(1). Suppress the message about the assumptions behind the calculations. Defaults to FALSE (recommended).

Value

A tibble with one row per stage, contingency type and block and columns:

stage, type, block

As in learning.

n_participants

Participants with at least one answered trial in the cell.

p_correct

Mean of the participants' p_correct.

se

Standard error of the p_correct mean, \(SD / \sqrt{n_{participants}}\); NA in rows with fewer than two participants.

Details

Every participant counts once per cell, no matter how many trials they answered. The standard error is computed between participants, because the learning check asks whether accuracy is above chance, not whether the accuracy differs as a function of cue type or stage (which would ask for a within-subjects SE instead). Every call states this definition of the standard error and states the cells where it could not be computed, unless silenced (silence = TRUE).

See also

score_learning(), plot_learning()
